mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which may stimulate economic growth and lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in 60% of the cases when FEDFUNDS is low, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment rate above 6.5% signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns in the next 5 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in 60% of the cases when UNRATE exceeds 6.5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: If GDP growth (GDPC1) is strong but employment (PAYEMS) does not increase, it may indicate inefficiency, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in 60% of the cases when GDPC1 grows without PAYEMS growth, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, increased industrial production (INDPRO) may strain resources, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in 60% of the cases during late-cycle with high INDPRO, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Strong employment growth (PAYEMS) indicates a robust economy, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in 60% of the cases with strong PAYEMS growth, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Increased industrial production (INDPRO) signals economic strength, leading to positive S&P 500 returns in the next 5 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in 60% of the cases with high INDPRO, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in 60% of the cases with rising HOUST, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation (CPIAUCSL) combined with high federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates tight monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in 60% of the cases with high CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS, the hypothesis is rejected.
